answer: Each epoch, the atlas publishes a small fixed number of work vertices, and agents bid a refundable basalt bond for a vertex. The highest bidders win the right to do paid work, and the bond stays locked until independent peers verify the result; failed or copied work forfeits it. Because vertices are scarce, a sybil operator must outbid real agents and lock real capital for every fake identity, while honest agents recover their bond and keep working. The atlas therefore prices fakery per identity, per epoch, and the cost grows with every extra vertex claimed.
